 Judgment
Challenging judgment and award dated 07.03.2017 passed by I Additional District Judge and MACT, Raichur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.119/2013, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: I Additional District Judge and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Smt.Chandrakala, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants, seeking enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that since insurer had not preferred appeal, finding of tribunal regarding occurrence of accident, involving insured vehicle, due to rash and negligent driving by its driver, resulting in death of Basavaraj, issuance of insurance policy and its coverage as on date of accident are not in dispute.

It was submitted that tribunal had assessed compensation of Rs.7,88,829/- and held owner i.e. respondent no.4 before tribunal liable to pay 25% and remaining 75% by Bajaj General Insurance Company Limited-respondent no.3- insurer of Jeep.
Even finding regarding contributory negligence / liability is also not in dispute.
It was submitted that as on date of accident i.e. 19.06.2012, deceased Basavaraj was 38 years of age and earning Rs.20,000/- per month from agriculture.

However, tribunal considered his monthly income notionally at Rs.6,000/-
and without adding future prospects awarded NC: 2023:KHC-K:7385 inadequate compensation.
It was also submitted that compensation awarded under conventional heads was meager and sought enhancement.
3. On other hand, Shri.Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for respondent no.3-insurer sought to support award.

4. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
5.

From above submission and since only claimants are in appeal, seeking enhancement, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
6.

Though claimants stated that deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from agriculture,
same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2012 is Rs.6,500/-.
Same has to be considered.
Claimants are wife and daughter.

As per ratio in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others,
claimants would be entitled for addition of 40% towards 'future NC: 2023:KHC-K:7385 prospects',
deduction towards personal expenses would be at '1/3rd' and multiplier applicable would be '15'.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, total loss of dependency would be:
(Rs.6,500 + 40% x 2/3 x 12 x 15) = Rs.10,92,000/-
7.

In addition, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, claimants being wife and daughter would be entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards 'loss of spousal consortium' and 'loss of filial consortium'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They would also be entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'.
9. Since three years have lapsed after rendering decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), claimants would be entitled for addition of 10% on compensation under conventional heads i.e., Rs.11,000/-.
Apart from above, tribunal awarded Rs.8,829/- towards medical expenses since death was during treatment.

Thus, claimants would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,21,829/- with interest at 6%
p.a.
Hence, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,21,829/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit, as against Rs.7,88,829/- awarded by Tribunal.
iii. Insurer shall deposit same within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
iv. Directions issued by tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release shall apply to enhanced compensation as per tribunal award.
